# Komatsu Deep Dive Analysis

Report 137 | Published 2024-05-26 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2024-5-26/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/137.json)

Komatsu value, monetary plumbing, and bitcoin models.

The ether-ETF timing, 2025 Fed turn and absence of a new mortgage-rate trough are supported. The report is appropriately skeptical of deterministic bitcoin price models. Komatsu valuation and EM rotation need independent relative-return testing; the thesis expressly allows a long wait.

**Coverage:** Entire report and chart inventory read; included policy timing, crypto politics, mining, model criticism, Komatsu, dollar-cycle exposure and mortgage transmission.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

The Desk announced $40 billion of initial bill purchases starting December 12, to maintain ample reserves. This is not itself evidence of deficit monetization as the causal motive.

### 137-C03

**Debt ceiling can release Treasury cash.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Ceiling binds in 2025 |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | debt-ceiling-tga-liquidity |
| Source blocks | 24, 25 |
| Thesis family | debt-ceiling-tga-liquidity |

The ceiling bound in 2025 and Treasury cash was drawn down, so this is no longer a pending scenario. The cash-release mechanism is supported, while the final reserve effect depends on the rest of the Fed balance sheet.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Fiscal2025 federal debt audit](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-107908) | GAO | 2026-01-20 | Verified in the audit

Debt ceiling reinstatedJanuary2 2025; extraordinary measuresJanuary21-July7; July4 law raised limit$5tn to$41.1tn. FY2025deficit$1.8tn.

- [Treasury cash observations](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WTREGEN) | FRED / Federal Reserve | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Weekly WTREGEN January 1, 2025 $719.873bn; April 9, 2025 $306.049bn, a $413.824bn drawdown during the extraordinary-measures period. Latest vintage downloaded November 7, 2026. Reserve effects also depend on other liabilities and assets.

### 137-C12

**Curve fits cannot determine bitcoin demand.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | bitcoin-model-uncertainty |
| Source blocks | 66, 106 |
| Thesis family | bitcoin-model-uncertainty |

Extrapolating past prices is not an identified demand model. Model fit alone cannot establish invariant future adoption or causal law; the earlier 2020 target is historical, not a fresh forecast.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Narrow deductive identity only; no empirical forecasting credit.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Deductive assessment:**

- Only a finite historical set of price observations is known
- No independently established structural demand restriction

Infinitely many functions fit the same finite observations yet diverge afterward. Historical fit alone therefore does not uniquely determine future prices.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.
